subject: Hiring charter & interview pattern — Senior Serving Engineer (EU)
messages:

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Hiring charter & interview pattern — Senior Serving Engineer (EU)

Team,

Quick planning note for the Priya Shah loop (Senior Serving Engineer, GH-7892). I want to align on role intent, a tight set of evaluation pillars, and who owns which interview segments so we present a consistent signal at debrief. Please see the attached resume and the evaluation rubric in the Drive.

Role intent (what success looks like at hire):
- Own critical parts of our GPU serving runtime for inference: latency budgets, KV cache correctness, and deployment stability at 99.95% SLO.
- Drive local performance experiments, quantify tradeoffs for batching/quantization, and ship reliable rollouts for model variants.
- Mentor junior engineers on inference patterns and observability.

Leveling expectations (senior vs staff quick callouts):
- Senior: owns end-to-end feature slices (design -> validation -> rollout) with guidance; clear signal on reducing p95/p99 latencies and root-cause analysis for regressions.
- Staff: leads cross-team initiatives, defines runtime-wide strategy (kernel selection, compiler choices), and sets measurable OKRs for throughput improvements.

Evaluation pillars (please keep to 4):
1) System design & tradeoffs — probes for scalability, batching, and failure modes.
2) Performance thinking — ability to quantify latency/cost tradeoffs and design experiments.
3) Debugging & root cause — live problem solving on logs/trace snippets.
4) Collaboration & communication — can they explain decisions to PMs/infra and land rollouts.

Suggested interview pattern (50–60m slots):
- System design (Marissa) — 20–25m: distributed KV/cache design, how to maintain correctness under eviction & sharding.
- Performance & micro-optimization (Markus) — 20m: latency budgets, batching strategies, quantization tradeoffs.
- Debugging exercise (peer) — 10–15m: given a short trace/log, find likely regressions and mitigation steps.
- Cultural / collaboration (we can fold into any slot) — 10m: cross-team communication, mentor examples.

Bar-raiser guidance: the bar-raiser should be looking for clear separation between measured/assumed tradeoffs, crisp experiment plans, and evidence of shipping and owning runtime-level changes (not just prototype PRs). We should call out any red flags (over-optimistic latency claims, no measurable outcomes from experiments).

Logistics / asks:
- Marissa: lead system design slot and own debrief score consolidation.
- Markus: please be bar-raiser or nominate someone who has recently owned performance rollouts.
- Naomi: please confirm candidate availability and send calendar invites once we lock slots.

Attachments: PriyaShah_resume.pdf, SeniorServing_eval_rubric.xlsx
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxxx/serving-hiring-pack
Greenhouse: GH-7892

Next steps: I propose we run interviews next week (Tue/Wed EU-friendly times). If folks have strong objections to the pillars or want to swap owners, speak up today.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Hiring Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sounds good — I can own the system design slot. A couple of quick asks:
- Add a short follow-up on rollout strategy / rollback patterns (5–7m) inside the system design slot. I want to hear concrete rollback hooks (feature flags, model pinning, traffic split).
- I'll use two targeted questions on cache sharding and consistency tradeoffs.

On the rubric: I think we should make the performance pillar explicit about p95 vs p99 and acceptable regressions (e.g., 10% transient vs sustained).

Onbar: happy to help synthesize scores and write the debrief summary.

Quick notes from my side:
- I can be the bar-raiser for this loop. I'll be explicitly scoring on (a) measurable experiment design, (b) system-level ownership evidence, and (c) clarity on tradeoffs.
- Please ensure the candidate can speak to concrete numbers — e.g., before/after improvements, latencies, batch sizes. If they cannot, that's fine, but we need to probe how they'd design an experiment to obtain those numbers.
- Add a one-slide prompt to the debugging exercise: short trace with a sudden p99 spike, partial traces, and a missing cache-miss counter. I will evaluate depth of investigation and mitigation prioritization.

Also request: can the panel get Priya's GitHub and any public notes (link in Drive would be fine) so I can see prior perf work? Naomi — can you ask the recruiter to surface that?
